items.title: [Articles - passivehouseplus.co.uk] Cairn comes good on high density passive house promise
items.content_html: Passive house has long been typecast as the preserve of deep-pocketed self-builders sold on the dream before pen hits paper. Now Ireland's largest housebuilder has smashed that assumption, delivering four passive schemes — and 1,755 homes — simultaneously, first time. And the real innovation may be what happened after the builders left: an unprecedented effort to prepare residents, housing staff and maintenance teams for life in a passive house — an effort led, in the interests of full disclosure, by this magazine's publishers.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Archohm: Indian Contemporary Architecture
items.content_html:
This publication compiles 25 years of work by Studio Archohm, highlighting their evolution into key players in Indian nation-building through large-scale urban, infrastructure, and civic projects, alongside private-sector experimentation.
The studio's multidisciplinary portfolio spans design research, city branding, education, and experience design, connecting scales from small objects to entire master plans. The featured projects seek to unlock space potential while balancing indigenous practices with global perspectives to reimagine a contemporary Indian design identity. Richly illustrated with plans, diagrams, and photography, the volume includes project breakdowns and essays from principals and international critics, capturing the firm's core philosophy to celebrate life through

items.title: [ArchDaily] Scalpers Headquarters / Estudio Hábito
items.content_html: The new Scalpers headquarters, located near Seville's Expo '92 site, is conceived as a building deeply rooted in its context and in the Andalusian architectural tradition, reinterpreted through a contemporary perspective.

items.title: [Architizer] The 14th A+Awards Projects of the Year: The Human Work Behind the Year’s Best Architecture
items.content_html:
Every season, the A+Awards surface thousands of remarkable buildings, and from among them Architizer’s editors single out a very small number as Projects of the Year. This year there are six. Read together, they share a common thread: in each, the central idea came out of the architects’ conversations with various stakeholders. And those dialogues…

items.title: [ArchDaily] Every Picture Tells a Story
items.content_html: Hand drawing is arguably architecture’s oldest “technology Even as we plunge headlong into the age of artificial intelligence, drawing remains a timeless, intuitive, and powerful medium for exploring. explaining, and understanding both built and imagined environments. A timeless tool for design thinking, hand drawing resonates on a deeply human level. This richly illustrated monograph features over 250 works from the 40-year career of architect Wesley L. Page, FAIA, ASAI, one of the nation’s top traditional media architectural illustrators. Rather than a “how-to” book of drawing tricks and techniques, it is a visual journal organized around a purpose-based approach to drawing

items.title: [ArchDaily] Bellano Cotton Mill Museum
items.content_html:
On the eastern shore of Lake Como in Bellano, Italy, the former Cantoni Cotton Mill tells a story of water, machinery and working life. Its substantial buildings and rhythmic façades offer a different perspective on a landscape more often associated with villas and waterfront gardens. The Bellano Cotton Mill Museum competition invites participants to give this industrial landmark a new cultural role.

Organised by Buildner in partnership with Selpi Srl, the competition asks participants to transform the smaller building within the complex into a museum and cultural destination. The task is to develop an architectural response that balances preservation with transformation,

items.title: [ArchDaily] "Earth Craft" at the U.S. Pavilion Will Trace the Work of Builders at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale
items.content_html: The United States' contribution to the 20th International Architecture Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia will explore the relationship between the country's architecture, landscapes, and the people who shape it. Titled Earth Craft, the exhibition will be commissioned, organized, and curated by a team from the University of Miami School of Architecture (U-SoA). The lead curator, Professor Germane Barnes, conceived the exhibition as a representation of the United States "through its makers and not through its icons," recognizing that celebrated buildings were raised by anonymous builders who dug, shaped, and fired architectural legacy. Vyta Pivo, assistant professor, curator, and historian of Earth Craft, adds a contemporary approach by translating inherited knowledge of soil, water, and heat into computational design, conceiving craftwork and robotic fabrication as complementary. The exhibition will occupy the United States Pavilion at the Giardini della Biennale between May 8 and November 21, 2027, tracing earthen materials from the ground to finished buildings.

items.title: [ArchDaily] House with Ghost Roof and Garden / OOOarchitecture
items.content_html: This wooden family home is located in a residential neighborhood in Inage Ward, Chiba City, Japan. The design is organized around an L-shaped, single-story plan that embraces a central garden. Rather than serving merely as an ancillary outdoor space, the garden forms the heart of the living environment, continually exposed to the changing conditions of light, wind, rain, and plant life.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Molina de Segura Pedestrian Bridge / FVAI
items.content_html: A new pedestrian and cycling connection transforms the boundary between the city, the agricultural landscape, and the Segura River into a public space for engaging with the surrounding landscape.

items.title: [Business Insider] I lost my tech job and couldn't afford my mortgage. Now I live in a 100-square-foot shed in the yard and rent out my house.
items.content_html: After a tech layoff, Lauren Patton couldn't afford her mortgage. So she built a tiny home and lives there while renting the main home on Airbnb.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Fuentesaúco Pharmacy / David Hernandez Arquitectura
items.content_html: The Fuentesaúco Pharmacy offers a reflection on the role of architecture in the recovery and modernization of essential services in rural areas. In a town of approximately 1,500 inhabitants, the project goes beyond renovating a commercial establishment to reaffirm the importance of maintaining nearby, accessible healthcare facilities that are connected to the everyday life of the community. In a context marked by population decline, architecture also becomes a tool for preserving quality of life and strengthening the community's identity.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Florian Residence 1 / Benthem Crouwel Architects
items.content_html: Florian Residence 1 is the first completed building and marks the beginning of a new urban district. Located on a prominent site near the National Bank of Slovakia, the building comprises eight floors, shops and amenities, and 73 homes ranging from compact studios to spacious apartments. High technological standards – triple glazing, high-performance thermal insulation, and acoustic engineering – ensure residents' optimal comfort, while the generous entrance and light-filled atrium lend the building an authentic sense of place and community.

items.title: [Dezeen] Five examples of Mesoamerican modern architecture
items.content_html:
Mexican architects have been combining principles from ancient architecture with modern techniques. Curator and writer Su Wu picks five examples of this phenomenon from her new book, Mesoamerican Modern.

items.title: [ArchDaily] House with Forest Windows / Yosuke Tomiya Architectural Design
items.content_html: House with Forest Windows is a compact timber residence in Sapporo, Hokkaido, located where an ordinary suburban neighborhood meets a dense woodland. The site offered an unusual condition: while neighboring houses stand close on the street side, the rear of the property opens directly toward the forest. The design began by asking how everyday family life could engage with this landscape while maintaining privacy from the surrounding residential environment.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Mila House / Isla Architects
items.content_html: The idea of renovating a mid-terrace home—tucked between a small street and an alley—changed radically when the opportunity arose to purchase the adjacent plot, a long, narrow strip measuring 25 meters long by just 2.5 meters wide, built edge to edge. This allowed for the creation of large openings onto the new courtyard, and the project transformed into an exploration of all possible ways to bring light into the homes: sliding windows flush with the wall exterior, vertical and horizontal pivoting panels, arched French doors, circular skylights, guillotine windows, and liftable panes.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Massó Apartment / Castroferro Arquitectura
items.content_html: Piso Massó approaches the renovation of a historic apartment in Vigo as an exercise in restoring those spatial qualities capable of continuing to respond to contemporary ways of living.

items.title: [MIT News] Fabric molds could bring material-saving concrete beams within reach
items.content_html:
🔧 🏔️ ✏️

MIT engineers cast a concrete beam using a sewn fabric mold with one-third the amount of concrete and half as much steel as a conventional beam.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Sertão Block and Amparo House / Asa Arquitetos
items.content_html: Located at Haras Amparo Medeiros, in the rural area of Princesa Isabel in the Paraíba hinterland (sertão), Casa Amparo was designed based on an analysis of the local natural conditions and landscape. The rugged topography, characterized by rocky outcrops, resilient vegetation, and open views of the territory, guided a layout that seeks to accommodate the architecture to the different levels, preserving the natural features of the site.

items.title: [ArchDaily] Restaurante Preta Maria / Estudio Guto Requena
items.content_html: An architectural project that celebrates Afro-Brazilian culture: this is the foundation of Preta Maria restaurant, designed by Estudio Guto Requena in collaboration with architects Gabriela de Matos and Mateus Fraga. Based on an Afrofuturist approach that breaks away from colonial representations of Africa, the project seeks to celebrate the experience of Africans in Brazil through architecture, art, technology, cuisine, and other forms of expression. Bamboo, rammed earth, stone, and high-tech resources such as parametric design come together in a composition that combines innovation, affection, and ancestry.
